title: Problem Formulation
text:
Problem Formulation
What is a Machine Learning Problem?
General Setting
• Given a dataset of input–output pairs:
D = {(xi, yi)}N
i=1
• Learn a function f (·) such that:
f (x) ≈y
• The function f is parameterized and learned from data
Machine learning is about learning a mapping from data, not writing explicit
rules.

title: Problem Formulation
text:
Problem Formulation
Training, Validation, and Test Sets
Dataset Splitting
• Training set: learn model parameters
• Validation set: tune hyperparameters, early stopping
• Test set: final unbiased evaluation
Important Rule
• Test data must NOT be used during training or tuning
• Avoid data leakage
Test set should be touched only once.

Output Space of Learning Tasks
Regression

• Vector output: y ∈RK
Classification
• Binary: y ∈{0, 1}
• Multi-class (single-label): y ∈{1, . . . , K}
• Multi-label: y ∈{0, 1}K
The output space determines activation functions and loss functions.

title: Problem Formulation
text:
Problem Formulation
Parametric Models and Inductive Bias
Parametric Model
• Model is defined as:
fθ(x)
• θ: learnable parameters (weights W , biases b)
Inductive Bias
• Built-in assumptions about the solution
• Examples:
• Linear models assume linear relationships
• CNN assumes locality and translation invariance
• Transformer assumes token interactions via attention
Learning is impossible without some form of inductive bias.
